newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak says Iran wanted him dead to dominate Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak says Iran wanted him dead to dominate Gulf.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said Iran helped the gunmen who tried to kill him in Addis Ababa last year because Egypt stood in the way of Iran occupying Arab land and dominating the Gulf states.

In an interview published on Wednesday, he backed one of his senior advisers, Osama el-Baz, who recently said that both Sudan and Iran took part in the plot to assassinate him on arrival in the Ethiopian capital in June 1995.

"There is information, the source for which is the confessions of the terrorists who were arrested. They confessed that Iran was involved and that it helped Sudan organise this operation," he told the London-based newspaper al-Hayat.
"Also, what's been published about the investigations conducted by the Ethiopian authorities...dealt with Iran's involvement in this," he added.
The gunmen were Egyptian members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest Islamist militant organisation trying to overthrow Mubarak and set up a strict Islamic state.
Asked what interest Iran had in this, Mubarak said: "Egypt stands as an obstacle to Iran's plans and its occupation of Arab territory and its ambitions to dominate the Gulf region."

Egypt and other Gulf states have repeatedly demanded Iranian withdrawal from three Gulf islands also claimed by the United Arab Emirates. Egypt has also accused Iran of helping incite the unrest of the past two years in Bahrain.
The full text of the interview with Mubarak was published in the Egyptian government newspaper al-Gomhuria.
